articles.standfirst: De ventiladores a máquinas de gelo, veja o que considerar antes de escolher os aparelhos para enfrentar os dias mais quentes.
articles.summary: De ventiladores a máquinas de gelo, veja o que considerar antes de escolher os aparelhos para enfrentar os dias mais quentes.
articles.body:
Verão 2026 começa em 21 de dezembro — Foto: Magnific

O verão está chegando e quem quer enfrentar os dias mais quentes com um pouco mais de conforto pode começar a se preparar desde já.

Ventilador, ar-condicionado, climatizador, máquina de gelo e até piscinas infláveis são algumas das opções para se refrescar e aliviar o calor.

O g1 reuniu as melhores reportagens e dicas do Guia de Compras para ajudar você a escolher entre diferentes alternativas. Confira a seguir.

Ar-condicionado do tipo inverter da LG — Foto: Divulgação

Aparelhos de ar-condicionado são o produto mais desejado quando se pensa em garantir o conforto térmico. Mas, entre modelos inverter, portáteis e de janela , é fácil se perder na hora de escolher.

Veja aqui um guia diferenciando cada modelo e entenda qual é o ideal para você ➡️ Onda de calor: saiba qual ar-condicionado escolher para se refrescar .

E atenção! Vale lembrar que nem todo condomínio permite a instalação desse tipo de aparelho, mesmo se tratando de modelos portáteis.

Mas, com um esforço em conjunto, os moradores têm a possibilidade de mudar isso. Saiba mais aqui ➡️ Por que alguns prédios proíbem a instalação de ar-condicionado?

Se não há perspectiva de instalar ar-condicionado no apartamento, a alternativa pode ser apostar em aparelhos menos eficientes, mas que ainda conseguem dar um alívio no calor.

O ventilador já é um velho conhecido dos brasileiros, com a função de circular o ar. Ele não diminui a temperatura da sala, mas gera uma brisa refrescante no ambiente. ➡️ Saiba como escolher entre ventilador de mesa ou de coluna .

Já os climatizadores são um meio-termo: não refrigeram tanto quanto um aparelho de ar-condicionado, mas são mais refrescantes que um ventilador comum . Eles são portáteis e usam um sistema de resfriamento com água e ventilação, sendo mais eficientes em tempo seco ➡️ Saiba como escolher e entenda como ele difere do ar-condicionado .

São aparelhos com capacidade de produzir entre 12 e 22 kg de gelo por dia, ideais para aquele dia de festa em casa em que a bandeja comum de gelo não dá conta do recado.

O Guia de Compras já testou três modelos dessa categoria, basta ler aqui ➡️ Máquina de gelo: g1 testa 3 modelos que aposentam as forminhas do freezer .

Crianças se refrescam em piscina inflável no bairro A.E. Carvalho, na Zona Leste de SP — Foto: EDI SOUSA/ATO PRESS/ESTADÃO CONTEÚDO

Se a vontade é aproveitar o sol e o calor dentro da piscina, mas você não tem acesso fácil a nenhuma, a solução pode ser adquirir um modelo inflável.

Para crianças, é importante ficar de olho nas recomendações de idade e manter supervisão constante. Veja mais orientações e opções de modelo aqui ➡️ Piscinas infláveis para crianças: o que os pais precisam saber antes de comprar .

E se a ideia é tentar montar uma piscina na varanda do apartamento ou no andar de cima de uma casa, cuidado! Não faça isso sem avaliação de um engenheiro para não causar acidentes . O volume de água da piscina é pesado e pode causar acidentes graves caso danifique a estrutura da edificação. Saiba mais aqui ➡️ Piscina inflável na varanda: saiba o que é preciso para instalar

articles.title: Meryl Streep’s former New York townhouse was built in 1845; the five-storey home featured six fireplaces and a rooftop garden
articles.summary: Meryl Streep’s former Greenwich Village home is a reminder of how much history can sit behind the red-brick façades of New York’s residential streets.
articles.body: Meryl Streep’s former Greenwich Village home is a reminder of how much history can sit behind the red-brick façades of New York’s residential streets. Built in 1845, the five-storey townhouse at 19 West 12th Street once belonged to the three-time Academy Award winner, who owned it for a decade before selling it in 2005. The property later changed hands twice before reaching the market with an asking price of $28.5 million in 2016, following a $6.5 million reduction. Spread across several levels, the house combines period architecture with a layout that includes six bedrooms, a rooftop garden and a substantial marble bathroom. Six fireplaces add another detail to its historic character.Inside Meryl Streep’s historic Greenwich Village townhouse with six fireplacesThe house stands on West 12th Street in Manhattan’s Greenwich Village, an area known for its older townhouses and residential blocks. Dating from 1845, the building was designed in the Late Greek Revival style, a form of architecture associated with the period’s interest in classical proportions and restrained ornament. Its red-brick exterior and narrow street frontage distinguish it from the larger apartment buildings found elsewhere in Manhattan.The property is 25 feet wide and extends across five storeys, with approximately 6,585 square feet of interior space, according to the estate details reported by Mansion Global in 2016. That vertical arrangement gives the house a series of separate living areas rather than a single expansive floor plan. Its six fireplaces are among the features associated with its historic residential design, while later fittings and amenities accommodate contemporary use.Meryl Streep’s former townhouse listed for $28.5 millionStreep purchased the townhouse in 1995 for $2.1 million. She retained ownership for ten years before selling it to Libet Johnson, an heiress to the Johnson & Johnson fortune, for $9.1 million in 2005. Johnson's ownership lasted only two years. In 2007, she sold the house for $12.8 million, and Elisabeth de Kergorlay, a countess and entrepreneur, acquired it in 2008 for $13.5 million, as reported by The Mansion Global.The succession of owners reflects the property's position in New York's high-end residential market. By September 2016, the townhouse was being offered for $28.5 million, down from an earlier asking price of $35 million that February. The reduction brought the advertised price $6.5 million lower, although the listing price alone did not establish what a future buyer might pay.Streep's connection to the house remained a central part of its appeal in property coverage. Her ownership, from 1995 to 2005, placed the residence among the private homes associated with one of Hollywood's most recognised actors. The building itself, however, predates her career by well over a century.The townhouse pairs a garden-facing terrace with six period fireplacesThe townhouse's interior was arranged to give different floors distinct purposes. The main entertaining rooms occupied the parlor level, where the living room and bar area sat alongside a formal dining room. From there, doors opened onto a terrace overlooking a garden, providing an outdoor space within the dense urban setting.At garden level, the house included a caretaker's apartment with its own kitchen, bathroom and bedroom. Higher up, the third floor contained a bedroom with an en-suite bathroom, as well as a sitting area and study. Two further bedrooms occupied the fourth floor, with a powder room in the hall. This distribution allowed the property to accommodate household staff, private working space and guest or family bedrooms without concentrating everything on the principal living floor.Six fireplaces formed part of the home's collection of period features. In a building constructed in the mid-19th century, such details offer a sense of its original domestic character, even as the rooms have been adapted for later owners. The available property report identifies the fireplaces as a feature but does not provide a room-by-room breakdown of their locations.The townhouse combines an expansive marble bathroom with skyline viewsThe top floor was devoted to the principal bedroom suite, which included a particularly large bathroom finished in Italian Calacatta marble. Reported to measure about 450 square feet, the bathroom stretched across the width of the townhouse. Its fittings included a cast-iron bathtub, a separate freestanding shower and a fireplace, combining the scale of a luxury bathroom with the older building's traditional architectural details.Above the house, a rooftop garden offered views across the city skyline. The basement provided additional storage and laundry space, leaving the main floors available for living, entertaining and sleeping. Together with the garden-level apartment and terrace, these features gave the property several outdoor and service areas despite its relatively narrow frontage.The townhouse’s asking price fell to $28.5 million in 2016The townhouse attracted renewed attention in 2016 when its asking price was reduced from $35 million to $28.5 million. Mansion Global reported that an open house had been scheduled for 3 October that year, with the Corcoran Group handling the listing. The property had therefore moved well beyond the prices paid by its earlier owners, at least in terms of its advertised value.The reported transaction history provides a clear sequence: Streep bought the house for $2.1 million in 1995, Johnson paid $9.1 million in 2005, another buyer acquired it for $12.8 million in 2007, and de Kergorlay paid $13.5 million in 2008. The $28.5 million figure was the property's asking price in 2016, not a confirmed sale price.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: Naga-Kuki clashes in Manipur: Kuki woman killed in Kamjong, severed head of Naga man found in Kangpokpi
articles.summary: Kuki-Zo woman killed in alleged Naga militant ambush in Manipur’s Kamjong; two missing. Severed head of Naga man found; home minister urges dialogue.
articles.body: GUWAHATI: A Kuki-Zo woman was killed and her husband injured in an alleged ambush by suspected Naga militants in Manipur’s Kamjong district on Thursday, while two other members of the community were reported missing as ethnic violence continued in the state.The deceased, Hatneikim Haokip, was from Molnoi village.Preliminary information suggests the group was travelling to Phaikoh to buy essential commodities when they were ambushed on the road between Phaikoh and Aishu. Hatneikim’s husband was injured, while the two other civilians who were with them remain missing.Thursday’s attack has taken the number of Kuki-Zo women killed in the Kuki-Naga clashes to 10, including two pregnant women. The clashes followed the Kuki-Meitei conflict that continued from 2023 to 2025.The attack came five days after nine people were killed across three districts, including two Kukis — one of them a woman — a Gorkha and six Naga men.Since the Kuki-Naga clashes began in Feb this year, at least 22 Naga and 32 Kuki-Zo people have been killed.Late on Wednesday night, security forces found the severed head of Naga man Ajinbou Ringkamai in Kangpokpi district. He was one of four Naga men killed when suspected Kuki militants attacked Makui Ashang village there on Oct 10. His head had been severed during the attack and remained missing. His headless body was taken to Jawaharlal Nehru Institute of Medical Sciences in Imphal on Oct 11.“The head was found in an isolated area near the site by security forces late on Wednesday night, and it was brought to JNIMS this morning for autopsy,” a senior official said.Joint Tribes Council Manipur, a Naga organisation, had given the authorities a 48-hour ultimatum to locate the head and ensure a proper funeral.Manipur home minister Govindas Konthoujam, speaking in Imphal on Thursday while visiting 84 BSF personnel admitted to Regional Institute of Medical Sciences with suspected food poisoning, said govt effort and security measures alone could not end the violence.“When the general people do not have humanity, then nobody can stop killing each other. We should understand that,” he said. “Killing will never solve any problem. We should talk to each other, and all differences should be resolved through dialogue.”He said govt was working to initiate dialogue but that society also had a role. “Security alone cannot solve the problem. We, the society and the people, should also try to restrain any kind of anger,” he said.Separately, Lt Gen Girish Kalia, General Officer Commanding of Spear Corps, visited an Assam Rifles forward post in Manipur on Thursday and reviewed the security situation. He was briefed on the preparedness of troops guarding India-Myanmar border.India shares a 1,643 km border with Myanmar, of which 398 km is in Manipur. Fencing has started, and nearly 55 km has been completed in the state. Govt plans to finish it by 2028. articles.title: Estudo no Brasil testa injeção contra HIV aplicada a cada 4 meses | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisa de fase 3 avalia se nova formulação consegue manter o vírus controlado com apenas três ciclos de aplicação por ano.
articles.summary: Pesquisa de fase 3 avalia combinação de cabotegravir e rilpivirina. Ativista Pisci Bruja foi a primeira participante no país a receber o esquema experimental.
articles.body:
Seringa e frasco de medicamento em imagem ilustrativa; estudo no Brasil testa tratamento injetável inédito contra HIV a cada 4 meses. — Foto: Pexels

Um estudo internacional em andamento no Brasil está testando um novo tratamento injetável contra o HIV que pode ser aplicado a cada quatro meses .

A pesquisa, chamada CUATRO , avalia versões de ação ultralonga de dois antirretrovirais, o cabotegravir e a rilpivirina .

💉 O objetivo é descobrir se o intervalo maior entre as aplicações consegue manter o HIV controlado com segurança e eficácia .

O estudo é de fase 3 , etapa em que um tratamento é avaliado em um número maior de participantes antes de uma eventual aprovação.

A previsão é reunir cerca de 564 voluntários em diferentes países . O acompanhamento deve seguir até 2029, embora os primeiros resultados principais sejam esperados antes disso.

No Brasil, 65 participantes já estão incluídos e outros cinco estão em processo de triagem , segundo o infectologista José Valdez Ramalho Madruga, pesquisador do Centro de Referência e Treinamento (CRT) em DST/Aids de São Paulo, um dos centros que participam da pesquisa.

No CRT, o recrutamento já foi encerrado . Ainda de acordo com Madruga, mais de 50 pessoas demonstraram interesse , mas apenas 11 puderam ser incluídas no estudo.

Entre as participantes da pesquisa está Pisci Bruja, antropóloga, pesquisadora, travesti e ativista pelos direitos das pessoas que vivem com HIV.

Doutoranda em Saúde Coletiva pela Faculdade de Medicina da USP, ela foi a primeira voluntária no Brasil a iniciar o braço da pesquisa que testa o intervalo de quatro meses e vê a participação também como uma forma de acompanhar de perto o desenvolvimento dessa nova opção de tratamento.

Pisci fala abertamente sobre viver com HIV e diz que, para ela, o tratamento diário ficou mais tranquilo ao longo dos anos, mas ressalta que essa não é a realidade de todas as pessoas .

“Tomar uma medicação todos os dias não é uma questão simples, principalmente por causa do estigma em torno do HIV. Muitas pessoas fazem isso escondidas, vão ao serviço de saúde escondidas e têm medo de que a sorologia seja exposta e de sofrer as consequências disso. Por isso, essa medicação injetável pode ser muito benéfica”, diz Pisci ao g1 .

A redução da frequência das doses é um dos principais pontos investigados por essas novas terapias de longa duração .

Além das questões sociais citadas por Pisci, os injetáveis podem ser uma alternativa para pessoas que têm intolerância aos medicamentos orais ou dificuldade de manter a rotina de tratamento .

"Tem a questão do esquecimento, mas também tem os fatores sociais. Às vezes, a pessoa não quer falar para o amigo, namorado ou namorada que tem HIV e precisa tomar medicação", afirma Madruga.

Nesse tipo de tratamento, o paciente vai ao serviço de saúde para receber as aplicações e retorna quando chega a data do ciclo seguinte.

"Assim, quanto maior o intervalo entre as doses, melhor para o paciente", acrescenta o infectologista.

Pisci Bruja, participante de estudo que testa um tratamento injetável contra o HIV aplicado a cada quatro meses. — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

O CUATRO não está testando pela primeira vez o uso do cabotegravir e da rilpivirina contra o HIV.

Os dois medicamentos já têm versões de ação prolongada estudadas e aprovadas em outros países para aplicações em intervalos menores.

A novidade é a tentativa de estender esse intervalo para quatro meses , usando novas formulações de ação ultralonga dos mesmos princípios ativos.

No grupo em que Pisci foi incluída, cada ciclo envolve duas injeções intramusculares : uma de cabotegravir e outra de rilpivirina.

Ela já recebeu o primeiro ciclo. O protocolo também prevê exames laboratoriais , eletrocardiogramas e um acompanhamento periódico para avaliar possíveis efeitos adversos e verificar se o vírus continua controlado.

A pesquisa inclui pessoas que já chegam ao estudo com carga viral suprimida. Isso significa que a nova formulação não está sendo avaliada como primeira opção para quem acabou de receber o diagnóstico, mas como uma alternativa para pacientes cujo tratamento já mantém o HIV controlado.

O principal indicador será a proporção de participantes que apresentar carga viral de 50 cópias por mililitro ou mais .

A comparação vai mostrar se as aplicações a cada quatro meses conseguem manter o HIV controlado com a mesma segurança e eficácia do esquema já existente.

Essa também é uma das limitações importantes ao interpretar o estudo: os resultados, se positivos, valerão inicialmente para um grupo específico de pacientes , já com o vírus controlado e que atendem aos critérios clínicos do protocolo.

Isso não significa, porém, que qualquer pessoa vivendo com HIV poderá trocar os comprimidos pelo esquema de três ciclos de aplicação por ano.

⚠️ O estudo ainda está em andamento e o acompanhamento dos participantes segue até 2029 .

Além disso, mesmo em fase 3, a nova formulação ainda precisa demonstrar que consegue manter o vírus controlado de forma segura antes de uma eventual aprovação.

Registro de uma transmissão colorizada de numerosas partículas do vírus HIV replicando-se a partir de uma célula T. — Foto: NIAID

Tratamento injetável ainda não está no SUS

As versões injetáveis de cabotegravir e rilpivirina já foram autorizadas pela Anvisa no Brasil para o tratamento de algumas pessoas que vivem com HIV, mas elas ainda não fazem parte do tratamento oferecido pelo Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS).

A oferta na rede pública depende de uma avaliação da Comissão Nacional de Incorporação de Tecnologias no SUS (Conitec) e de decisão do Ministério da Saúde.

Hoje, o SUS oferece principalmente esquemas de antirretrovirais de uso diário. Eles mantêm o vírus controlado e podem levar a carga viral a níveis indetectáveis. Quando isso ocorre de forma sustentada, a pessoa não transmite o HIV por via sexual, princípio conhecido como I=I, Indetectável = Intransmissível.

A proposta dos tratamentos de longa duração é ampliar essas opções e reduzir a frequência das doses.

No caso do CUATRO, a pesquisa tenta descobrir se é possível aumentar para quatro meses o intervalo entre as aplicações sem comprometer o controle do HIV.

Mas mesmo que os resultados sejam positivos, a nova formulação ainda precisará passar por avaliação regulatória e, para chegar ao SUS, por um processo específico de incorporação.

articles.title: Filha de Elize Matsunaga não estava na mansão invadida por ladrões | G1
articles.standfirst: Imóvel pertence aos pais de Marcos, empresário assassinado e esquartejado pela mulher, Elize, em 2012. Três funcionários foram feitos reféns. PM de SP matou 3 suspeitos do roubo.
articles.summary: Imóvel pertence aos pais de Marcos, empresário assassinado e esquartejado pela mulher, Elize, em 2012. Três funcionários foram feitos reféns. PM matou 3 suspeitos.
articles.body:
Elize e Marcos Matsunaga com a filha. — Foto: Reprodução/Arquivo pessoal

A filha de Elize Matsunaga e os pais de Marcos Matsunaga não estavam na mansão da família do empresário quando ela foi invadida por pelo menos quatro assaltantes armados na tarde de quarta-feira (14), em Pinheiros, na Zona Oeste de São Paulo, segundo policiais ouvidos pelo g1 . Três funcionários que estavam na residência foram feitos reféns e resgatados pela Polícia Militar.

A tentativa de roubo terminou com três suspeitos do roubo mortos em confronto com a PM, um homem de 39 anos preso em flagrante pelo crime e um policial ferido no ombro. Não há confirmação se havia mais criminosos participando do assalto. Também não foi informado se algum bem foi levado.

De acordo com policiais, o imóvel invadido pela quadrilha pertence a Mitsuo Matsunaga e Misako Kitano, pais de Marcos Matsunaga, empresário assassinado e esquartejado pela esposa, Elize Matsunaga, em maio de 2012 . O crime foi cometido no apartamento em que o casal morava com a filha, em outro endereço na Zona Oeste. Na época, Marcos era um dos diretores da empresa de alimentos Yoki.

Desde o assassinato, a filha de Marcos e Elize passou a morar com os pais do empresário, que são octogenários. Os avós e a neta, uma adolescente de 15 anos, não estavam na residência no momento do roubo, segundo os policiais.

Segundo a Secretaria da Segurança Pública (SSP), a PM foi acionada para atender à ocorrência e deteve um dos suspeitos no pavimento térreo da casa. Em seguida, os agentes localizaram outros três suspeitos, e houve confronto. Dois deles morreram no local. O terceiro foi encaminhado à Unidade de Pronto Atendimento (UPA) Lapa, mas não resistiu aos ferimentos.

O policial militar atingido no ombro foi levado ao Hospital das Clínicas, onde permaneceu sob cuidados médicos. As armas foram apreendidas, e a perícia foi acionada.

O homem preso permaneceu à disposição da Justiça. O caso foi registrado como roubo a residência no 14º Distrito Policial (DP), Pinheiros, que solicitou apoio do Departamento de Homicídios e Proteção à Pessoa (DHPP). A PM também abriu um Inquérito Policial Militar (IPM) para apurar a atuação dos agentes.

Elize Matsunaga, acusada de matar o marido, o empresário Marcos Kitano Matsunaga, em foto de junho de 2012 quando foi levada ao DHPP em São Paulo para prestar depoimento — Foto: Nilton Fukuda/Estadão Conteúdo/Arquivo

A residência da família Matsunaga já havia sido alvo de outro roubo em agosto de 2023. Na ocasião, Mitsuo Matsunaga, a mulher dele e a neta foram rendidos por três criminosos armados com faca durante a madrugada. À época, eles amarram as vítimas e fugiram, roubando R$ 20 mil em dinheiro, joias, celulares e duas armas em nome de Mitsuo.

Mitsuo Matsunaga, pai de Marcos, é um empresário ligado à Yoki, fabricante de alimentos que fez parte dos negócios da família. De origem japonesa e naturalizado brasileiro, ele é genro de Yoshiro Kitano, fundador da antiga empresa Kitano, que passou a se chamar Yoki em 1990.

Elize Matsunaga foi condenada por matar Marcos Matsunaga em 2012. — Foto: Reprodução/Arquiivo pessoal

Mitsuo esteve à frente do grupo familiar até a venda da companhia por quase R$ 1,95 bilhão para a multinacional norte-americana General Mills em 2012.

Em 2025, Mitsuo apareceu na 189ª posição da lista de bilionários brasileiros da Forbes, com patrimônio estimado em R$ 2 bilhões. A fortuna está ligada à trajetória empresarial da família no setor de alimentos.

Além da atuação nos negócios, Mitsuo e a mulher, Misaki Kitano, assumiram a criação da neta após a morte de Marcos. A adolescente tinha cerca de 1 ano quando o pai foi assassinado.

O g1 tenta contato com a família Matsunaga para comentar o assunto.

Marcos foi morto em 19 de maio de 2012, aos 42 anos. Elize confessou ter atirado na cabeça do marido e, depois, desmembrado o corpo em sete partes. Os restos mortais foram encontrados na região de Cotia, na Grande São Paulo.

Ela alegou ter agido sob forte emoção durante uma discussão, depois de descobrir uma traição do marido. Segundo sua versão, Marcos a agrediu e ameaçou matá-la e tirar dela a guarda da filha do casal.

Em dezembro de 2016, Elize foi condenada pelo júri a 19 anos e 11 meses de prisão por homicídio qualificado, destruição e ocultação de cadáver. Em 2019, o Superior Tribunal de Justiça (STJ) reduziu a pena para 16 anos e três meses.

Em maio de 2022, após cumprir cerca de dez anos de prisão, Elize deixou a Penitenciária de Tremembé, no interior de São Paulo, em liberdade condicional.

Na ocasião, ela afirmou num vídeo ao lado de seu advogado, Luciano Santoro (veja acima) :

“Infelizmente não posso consertar o que se passou, o erro que cometi. Estou tendo uma segunda chance, infelizmente o Marcos não. Mas eu acredito na espiritualidade, que ele já tenha me perdoado e peço isso todas às vezes em minhas orações”, disse Elize.

Atualmente, Elize, que tem 44 anos, tenta retomar o contato com a filha por meio da Justiça.

articles.title: iPhone Duo entra em pré-venda nesta sexta; veja preços do dobrável | G1
articles.standfirst: Primeiro dobrável da empresa foi lançado em setembro junto com os iPhone 18 Pro e Pro Max. Novo aparelho será entregue a partir de 23 de outubro.
articles.summary: Primeiro dobrável da empresa foi lançado em setembro junto com os iPhone 18 Pro e Pro Max. Novo aparelho será entregue a partir de 23 de outubro.
articles.body:
O iPhone Duo, primeiro celular dobrável da Apple , entrou em pré-venda nesta sexta-feira (16). O novo aparelho, que foi lançado em setembro , é vendido no site da Apple por até R$ 30.999 e ser entregue pela empresa a partir de 23 de outubro. (veja preços abaixo)

Principal novidade do evento realizado pela Apple em setembro, o iPhone Duo marca a entrada da empresa em um segmento já explorado por concorrentes como Samsung e Huawei.

O novo celular tem tela externa de 5,4 polegadas , que permite acessar vários recursos do iOS, e tela interna de 7,6 polegadas , cerca de 80% maior que a do iPhone 18 Pro, segundo a Apple.

Para funcionar com duas telas, o aparelho é fabricado com uma dobradiça equipada com 100 peças. A Apple diz que o componente foi projetado para oferecer abertura e fechamento suaves.

A empresa usou titânio na carcaça do iPhone Duo e aplicou uma textura à tela interna para reduzir o vinco que costuma aparecer no uso de celulares dobráveis.

A tela interna promete oferecer mais produtividade para usuários e permite abrir, ao mesmo tempo, apresentações e chamadas de vídeo, por exemplo.

Já a tela externa consegue mostrar informações rápidas no modo de espera. Ela pode ser usada como um despertador, um porta-retratos, uma tela com previsão do tempo, entre outros.

O modelo tem duas câmeras de 48 megapixels, uma de 12 megapixels na área externa, além de uma câmera para chamadas de vídeo que fica oculta quando não está em uso.

O iPhone Duo será vendido nas cores chamadas pela Apple de branco-estrela e céu noturno. Ele se junta aos iPhone 18 Pro e Pro Max, que já estão sendo vendidos desde setembro. Confira abaixo os preços do celular dobrável da Apple.

O iPhone Duo usa o mesmo chip A20 Pro dos iPhone 18 Pro e Pro Max, lançados nesta quarta-feira.

Por conta do novo visual, a Apple retomou o uso do Touch ID, seu leitor de impressões digitais, para desbloquear o aparelho. Nos modelos convencionais do iPhone, a empresa costuma usar apenas o Face ID, de reconhecimento facial, como recurso de biometria.

E, assim como o iPhone Air, modelo compacto lançado em 2025, o iPhone Duo terá suporte apenas para o eSIM, sem uma porta para chips físicos.

O celular tem proteção Ceramic Shield, que oferecem mais proteção contra quedas e certificação IP68, que garante resistência a respingos, água e poeira.

articles.title: O que Renato Russo estaria fazendo hoje? Companheiros de Legião Urbana falam do amigo, 30 anos depois de sua morte | G1
articles.standfirst: Líder da Legião Urbana e autor de algumas das canções mais marcantes do rock nacional, Renato segue sendo lembrado não apenas pela obra que deixou, mas também pela personalidade e pela forma como enxergava o mundo.
articles.summary: Líder da Legião Urbana e autor de algumas das canções mais marcantes do rock nacional, Renato segue sendo lembrado não apenas pela obra que deixou, mas também pela personalidade e pela forma como enxergava o mundo.
articles.body:
Trinta anos após a morte de Renato Russo, a influência do cantor e compositor continua presente na música brasileira. Líder da Legião Urbana e autor de algumas das canções mais marcantes do rock nacional, Renato segue sendo lembrado não apenas pela obra que deixou, mas também pela personalidade e pela forma como enxergava o mundo.

Em reportagem exibida pelo Fantástico, os músicos Dado Villa-Lobos e Marcelo Bonfá, parceiros de Renato na Legião Urbana, relembraram histórias do amigo e refletiram sobre o legado que atravessa gerações. Veja a reportagem completa acima.

Descrito pelos companheiros como alguém de vasta cultura e senso crítico apurado, Renato era, nas palavras de Dado, uma espécie de "livraria absurda de textos e música". Já Bonfá destacou o humor refinado e a inteligência do cantor, características que ajudaram a moldar uma das obras mais influentes da música brasileira.

Carioca criado em Brasília, Renato Russo transformou experiências pessoais, reflexões políticas e questões existenciais em letras que continuam encontrando novos ouvintes décadas depois. Canções como "Tempo Perdido", "Pais e Filhos", "Eduardo e Mônica" e "Faroeste Caboclo" seguem entre as mais conhecidas do repertório do grupo.

Para Dado Villa-Lobos, a permanência dessas músicas está ligada à capacidade de Renato de escrever sobre temas universais. Segundo ele, o compositor buscava criar letras que pudessem ser compreendidas em diferentes épocas e lugares, evitando referências excessivamente datadas. Isso ajudou a transformar suas canções em obras que continuam atuais para públicos de diversas gerações.

A força da conexão de Renato com o público também foi um dos pontos lembrados pelos ex-companheiros de banda. No palco, ele tinha um poder de comunicação raro. "Parecia que ele estava cantando para você", recordou Bonfá ao falar sobre a capacidade do cantor de transformar letras pessoais em experiências coletivas.

Ao longo da entrevista, Dado e Bonfá destacaram que a Legião Urbana deixou uma obra com relevância ética, estética, poética e cultural, capaz de dialogar com diferentes momentos da sociedade brasileira. Para Bonfá, a lembrança de Renato permanece viva não apenas entre amigos e familiares, mas também entre milhões de admiradores que continuam redescobrindo suas músicas.

Renato Russo morreu em 11 de outubro de 1996, aos 36 anos, vítima de complicações decorrentes da aids. Três décadas depois, suas composições continuam ocupando espaço em playlists, programas de TV e apresentações musicais.

Questionado sobre o que imaginava para o amigo caso ele estivesse vivo, Bonfá não hesitou na resposta. Para o músico, Renato seguiria fazendo aquilo que mais amava.

"Ele estaria fazendo o que ele sempre fez melhor, que é compor, fazer músicas e cantar", afirmou.

Para os companheiros de Legião Urbana, é justamente essa produção artística que mantém Renato Russo presente. Trinta anos após sua morte, a trajetória do cantor reforça uma ideia repetida ao longo da reportagem: o artista pode ser mortal, mas a arte permanece.

articles.body: TOI correspondent from London: A 41-year-old Romanian neighbour of the three Indian students killed in a fire in west Germany has been arrested on suspicion of their murder.The man, who lived in the same apartment block as the students, is being held in pre-trial detention and is being questioned by homicide detectives, Bochum police said. The man was already known to police for assault and property offences. Formal charges have not yet been filed.There had also been a police operation at the same apartment block on Sunday involving a dispute, German media reported.Two female and one male Indian student, all in their 20s and from Kerala, were killed in the fire which broke out in an apartment building on Poststraße, in the Hofstede district of Bochum, North Rhine-Westphalia, at 4.15 am Tuesday. Their bodies were found in an apartment on the second floor. Five people were injured and taken to hospital.When the fire brigade arrived, the flames had already spread throughout the building. Residents said several strollers in the hallway had been set alight, causing the fire to spread to the wooden staircase, blocking the only escape route and preventing firefighters from rescuing people via the stairs. Many residents had to escape through windows. A cat, too, was rescued, given oxygen treatment, and handed over to a veterinarian.Chittranjan Dubey, an Indian national living in Germany, told TOI: “Racism against Indians is increasing each year and the German state needs to intervene before it’s too late.”You use AI every day. articles.body: TOI correspondent from London: A British Bangladeshi civil servant is on trial in the UK accused of fraudulently taking on five full-time govt jobs at the same time which he juggled by taking sick leave and working remotely without switching his camera on.Kashim Chowdhury (55) of Whitechapel, East London, is alleged to have earned almost £350,000 (Rs 4.4 crore) per year from multiple public sector roles between Feb 2020 and Sept 2023.These included the home office, the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra), the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) and the Department of Health and Social Care.At one point he was contracted to work 183 hours a week for five roles — more hours than exist in seven days.Chowdhury, on trial at Southwark Crown Court charged with nine counts of fraud, which he denies, often used sick leave to hide his other employment from managers, the court heard. articles.title: 56 year old Chestnut trees, said to be one of America’s last remaining Chestnut Groves, at risk of being wiped out by datacenter labelled as: 'One of the largest single AI infrastructure investments in US history'
articles.summary: In 1904, a necrotrophic fungus called chestnut blight began devastating North America's native chestnut trees.
articles.body: In 1904, a necrotrophic fungus called chestnut blight began devastating North America's native chestnut trees. This fungus, brought across the Pacific on chestnut trees from Japan and China, attacks tree bark and kills the above-ground portions of susceptible trees. The disease eventually wiped out billions of chestnut trees across the US. More than a century later, a grove of approximately 200 blight-resistant American chestnut trees in West Virginia is facing the threat of being cleared to make way for a large-scale artificial intelligence data center.​Planted in the 1970s, the 56-year-old trees are a valuable source of genetic material that could help restore the species. However, the proposed Monarch Compute Campus, developed by Nscale in collaboration with Nvidia and Caterpillar, could put the grove at risk. The project is planned to span more than 2,250 acres and provide 8 gigawatts of computing capacity, with its developer calling it “one of the largest single AI infrastructure investments in US history.”​Why the West Virginia chestnut grove matters​The chestnut blight outbreak destroyed an estimated 4 billion American chestnut trees across the US. Although surviving stumps can produce new shoots, these often succumb to the disease before reaching maturity.​Researchers and horticulturists have since worked to preserve the species through breeding programmes and blight-resistant hybrids. However, mature chestnut groves remain uncommon. According to the supplied report, fewer than 4,300 acres of fruit-producing chestnut trees existed across the continental US in 2023.​The grove contains about 200 blight-resistant chestnut trees planted in the 1970s from surviving wild American chestnuts. Their age and genetic material make them a potentially important resource for future restoration efforts.​A report published in From the Front Lines: Struggles for Justice by the New York-based Global Justice Ecology Project has raised concerns about the grove's future.​“Planted in the 1970s from wild surviving American chestnuts, this orchard is a vital ‘genetics library,'” the publication explains, describing it as “the primary seed source to restore the species across West Virginia.”​The trees could provide seeds and genetic material for efforts to establish new chestnut populations. Losing the grove could therefore affect more than the existing trees, potentially reducing the resources available to future restoration projects.​What is the Monarch Compute Campus​The proposed data center development is being built by Nscale in collaboration with Nvidia and Caterpillar. Under the current plans, the completed campus will cover more than 2,250 acres and provide 8 gigawatts of computing capacity for AI companies, including Anthropic.​The development represents a substantial investment in computing infrastructure as technology companies expand their capacity to train and run artificial intelligence models.​Nscale has described the project as “one of the largest single AI infrastructure investments in US history, anchoring America’s compute foundation.”​The scale of the planned facility could make protecting the grove difficult, especially if the trees fall within areas designated for construction.​A conflict between AI infrastructure and conservation​The potential loss of the chestnut grove highlights a conflict between expanding AI infrastructure and preserving biological resources. Data centers require large sites, electricity and supporting infrastructure, while conservation projects depend on protecting habitats and maintaining genetic diversity.​According to From the Front Lines, the surviving chestnut trees are “irreplaceable” because they could support future restoration work.​The grove's future will depend on the development plans and whether its preservation can be reconciled with construction. For conservationists, protecting these trees could help retain an important source of genetic material for restoring American chestnuts to their former range.You use AI every day. articles.title: An Oklahoma zoologist built an 80-foot blue whale beside a pond for his grandchildren; the concrete roadside landmark became a Route 66 attraction
articles.summary: Beside a quiet pond in Oklahoma, an enormous blue whale rises from the grass, and travellers have been stopping to admire it for decades.
articles.body: Beside a quiet pond in Oklahoma, an enormous blue whale rises from the grass, and travellers have been stopping to admire it for decades. The Blue Whale of Catoosa began as a grandfather's gift, a playful, welcoming structure meant to give his grandchildren a place to swim and play. Today it stands as one of the most cherished stops along historic Route 66, drawing families, curious travellers, and road trip enthusiasts from all over. This article explains who built the whale, how the work was done, why the landmark endures, and what you should know before planning your own visit.Hugh Davis, the Oklahoma zoologist and devoted grandfather who sketched a giant whale for his familyThe story begins with a scientist who was also a devoted family man. According to the City of Catoosa's official page about the landmark, the whale was originally built by Hugh Davis, a zoologist who imagined it as a special place where his grandchildren could play and swim in the nearby pond. In other words, this enormous roadside giant started as an act of affection rather than a business plan. The City of Catoosa told visitors on that page that his sketches of the mammal kept growing until the design reached 20 feet tall and 80 feet long. That is a remarkable leap for a drawing that began as a family idea, and it explains why the finished whale feels so personal, welcoming, and unlike the polished attractions found elsewhere along the highway.How two friends welded a metal frame and hand-mixed cement by the bucket to create the Catoosa whaleTurning a sketch into a structure took patience, muscle, and a good friend. The City of Catoosa told visitors that Davis worked with a friend named Harold Thomas, and together the two men spent two years welding the metal framework that gave the whale its shape. Once the skeleton finally stood ready, they covered it with hand-mixed cement, applying it one five-gallon bucket at a time. Imagine the effort involved, every curve of the body, from the tail to the wide smile, was built up slowly and patiently through repeated trips with heavy buckets. The city's page states that the whale was completed in July 1972, which means this beloved landmark has now welcomed travellers for more than five decades.From family swimming hole to beloved Route 66 roadside attraction: What visitors can do at the whaleAlmost as soon as it was finished, the whale began pulling in crowds. After its completion in July 1972 the structure attracted people from all over, and the pond became a place where they swam, fished, and picnicked. Times have changed in one important way, the city notes that swimming in the pond is no longer allowed. You can still pack a picnic lunch, cast a line for a day of fishing, or feed the turtles, and restroom facilities are available on site. The City of Catoosa owns and operates the park, and its page describes the area as a family favorite for generations and a must-see for any traveler on Route 66.Television series and advertisements which made the Blue Whale of Catoosa a famous Oklahoma landmarkFame arrived well beyond the highway itself. The City of Catoosa's page lists the whale among the subjects featured in the comic strip Zippy the Pinhead and in the British television series An Idiot Abroad, in the second season's sixth episode. It also appeared on The Great Food Truck Race, in the fifth episode of the sixth season titled Roadside Attractions, and on American Pickers in an episode called On the Road Again. Advertising took notice as well, with a 2019 Mercedes-Benz television commercial titled Attractions and a Phillips 66 commercial from the Live to the Full series. The city credits Wikipedia for this list, so readers wanting even more detail can follow the link in the sources listed below.Planning your visit to the Blue Whale of Catoosa: Location, opening hours, free admission, and toursThe City of Catoosa lists the location as 2600 United States Route 66, Catoosa, Oklahoma 74015. Opening hours are Sunday from eleven in the morning until four in the afternoon; Monday through Wednesday from nine in the morning until four in the afternoon; Thursday from nine in the morning until seven in the evening; and Friday and Saturday from nine in the morning until four in the afternoon. Admission is free, and both guided and self-guided tours are available. Groups must reserve in advance and can use motorcoach parking. The city also announced renovations planned for summer 2025, so contact the park before you travel to confirm current conditions.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Israeli firm used online ads to run vast spy operation, researchers say
articles.summary: Israeli digital advertising agency Discover-Tech used a sprawling network of online ads to identify and track internet users and help hack their devices,
articles.body: Israeli digital advertising agency Discover-Tech used a sprawling network of online ads to identify and track internet users and help hack their devices, Canadian cyber watchdog Citizen Lab and New York advertising security firm Confiant said on Thursday. Its services gave Israeli spyware firm Candiru and other surveillance companies access to ad platforms run by Google, Comcast, Yandex and others.The reports said the online advertising industry, already under scrutiny over privacy, could serve as a channel for extensive espionage. Discover-Tech's ads, often promoting ordinary products such as phones or earpods, reached more than 120,000 websites and 75,000 apps through its partnerships, Citizen Lab said.Users visiting sites or using apps carrying the malicious ads could be identified and tracked by Discover-Tech, which sometimes tried to extract phone numbers from smartphone users, researchers said. The ads only had to load for the surveillance to occur. Some also helped install Candiru spyware on devices, although Confiant said these made up a tiny fraction of Discover-Tech's volume.Confiant co-founder Jerome Dangu said Discover-Tech distributed at least 10 million ads daily worldwide and used data-sharing arrangements known as cookie matching to track people beyond their reach. "Very likely hundreds of millions of people would have been touched by Discover-Tech," Dangu said.Discover-Tech, founded in 2020, did not respond to messages, while attempts to reach chief executive Dekel Boni and Candiru's owners were unsuccessful. US commerce department blacklisted Candiru in 2021, alleging it supplied spyware used to maliciously target govt officials, journalists, activists and academics.Citizen Lab said Candiru spyware delivered through Discover-Tech ads compromised 45 Windows devices at Qatari broadcaster Al Jazeera between 2024 and 2025. It said it confirmed the attacks using network logs shared by the broadcaster. Al Jazeera did not respond.Dangu said malicious ads appeared on hundreds of networks in sensitive categories, including Pentagon, International Atomic Energy Agency and International Criminal Court. He said Palestinian territories were particularly saturated, adding: "You go to almost any site in Palestine - any site - you find a Discover-Tech ad. It gives them a very complete visibility on the digital activities of an entire country," he said.Citizen Lab said it had similar evidence that the ads were shown to people in UN, Nato, European Commission and more than a dozen national govts. They also appeared on networks of chip companies including Nvidia, Sandisk, Broadcom and Micron, and unidentified media organisations in Mexico, Israel and Europe.Google said it had worked with both investigators and removed Discover-Tech from its ad platforms "for systematically violating our policies." IAB Europe suspended it from its approved-vendor list after an audit, while Comcast subsidiary Beeswax removed it from its platform. Yandex did not respond.You use AI every day. articles.title: England transformed an unused wastewater tank into a floating wetland with 3,296 plants, while scientists prepare to test its water-cleaning ability
articles.summary: An unused wastewater tank in Somerset, England, has been repurposed as a floating wetland designed to improve water quality and create habitat for
articles.body: An unused wastewater tank in Somerset, England, has been repurposed as a floating wetland designed to improve water quality and create habitat for wildlife. In May 2026, Biomatrix Water worked with YTL Construction UK to install 275 square metres of floating wetlands at Cheddar Water Recycling Centre for Wessex Water. The floating wetland sits on a retired aeration ditch and consists of 82 interlocking modules supporting 3,296 aquatic plants. Their submerged roots provide surfaces for microbial communities that can help remove pollutants from water. The installation is intended to improve the quality of water from stormwater overflows before it reaches a nearby watercourse. Within 3 months, a pair of ducks had also settled on the wetland and raised a brood, according to Biomatrix Water. However, the site’s treatment performance has yet to be established through water sampling.Floating wetland at Cheddar Water Recycling Centre: how 82 modules support 3,296 plantsThe project was constructed and installed by Biomatrix Water, with engineering services provided by Mott MacDonald, working alongside YTL Construction UK on behalf of Wessex Water. Rather than removing the retired aeration ditch, the team adapted it to support a nature-based treatment system. Biomatrix Water says the installation covers 275 square metres and uses its Geomatrix design, made up of 82 interlocking modules. Together, these support 3,296 aquatic plants.The plants’ roots hang into the water and provide surfaces for biofilm to develop. Biofilm is a community of microorganisms, including bacteria, algae and fungi, that grows on submerged surfaces. These organisms can contribute to the breakdown and transformation of organic matter and nutrients in water. The floating structure allows the plants to grow above the water while their roots remain in contact with it. The system is intended to improve water quality before stormwater overflows leave the site and reach a watercourse. It is important, however, to distinguish the wetland’s intended function from measured results. Alistair Barlow of YTL Construction UK said, in comments quoted in Biomatrix Water’s September 10, 2026, case study, that water samples would be taken at the inlet and outlet to assess the wetland’s performance. Biomatrix Water’s Nick Schreiner also said sampling was starting at that point. The results had not yet been reported in the case study. Floating treatment wetlands: what scientific research saysThe underlying technology has been studied beyond Somerset. A 2021 review published in Science of the Total Environment, titled Application of floating treatment wetlands for stormwater runoff: A critical review of the recent developments with emphasis on heavy metals and nutrient removal, examined how floating treatment wetlands can help manage stormwater pollution. Researchers Rozi Sharma, Jan Vymazal and Piyush Malaviya described how plants growing on floating rafts and biofilms attached to their submerged roots contribute to pollutant removal. The review examined the potential for these systems to remove nutrients and heavy metals and discussed the role of hydraulics and other design parameters in treatment performance.A second review, published in Applied Sciences in 2025, is titled The Bioremediation of Nutrients and Heavy Metals in Watersheds: The Role of Floating Treatment Wetlands. It examines floating treatment wetlands used in settings including stormwater, agricultural runoff and wastewater. The authors identify factors such as the time water spends in the system, the thickness of the floating mat, plant species and microbial interactions as important influences on treatment performance. The review also highlights seasonal variation and the need to evaluate systems under different operating conditions. These findings provide scientific context for the Cheddar installation, but they do not establish how effectively that particular wetland will perform. Its inlet and outlet measurements will be needed to assess changes in water quality under local conditions, including variations in weather and water flow.Reusing a retired aeration ditch The Cheddar installation is also an example of adapting existing infrastructure instead of removing it. Biomatrix Water explains that treatment works are periodically upgraded, leaving older tanks and other assets redundant. Removing them can be expensive, so some structures remain unused. Retrofitting such a space with floating wetlands offers another option: an existing asset can be adapted to support a nature-based treatment system. The approach is not entirely new for Wessex Water. In 2024, the company worked with Biomatrix Water on a floating wetland at Ubley Water Recycling Centre in Bristol. That earlier project was installed in a stormwater lagoon as part of a trial to assess whether nature-based solutions could improve the quality of stormwater overflows at sites affected by high groundwater infiltration. The project description said water sampling would be used to assess changes in quality before water entered a local stream.At Cheddar, the wildlife response provides an early sign that the floating structure is offering habitat. Biomatrix Water reported that a pair of ducks settled there and raised a brood within 3 months of installation. That observation is distinct from evidence of water-treatment effectiveness, which remains to be measured. The next stage is therefore monitoring. Samples taken at the wetland’s inlet and outlet can help establish whether water quality changes as water passes through the system. Those results will be important in determining the installation’s performance and informing decisions about similar projects. For now, Cheddar demonstrates how a retired wastewater structure can be repurposed for a new ecological use, while the extent of its contribution to water treatment awaits measurement.You use AI every day. articles.summary: A 52-year-old Russian national has been extradited from Sweden to the United States to face federal charges over an alleged international scheme to
articles.body: A 52-year-old Russian national has been extradited from Sweden to the United States to face federal charges over an alleged international scheme to procure American electronic components for Russia in violation of US export restrictions, authorities said Thursday.Alexander Suvorov is accused of using companies in Hong Kong to purchase US-made technology with potential military applications and conceal its intended shipment to Russia. The components could be used in military communications, radar systems, drones and precision navigation equipment, according to federal investigators.Suvorov faces three federal conspiracy charges involving international money laundering, outbound smuggling and violations of the Export Control Reform Act.“They are technologies that the United States strictly controls because in the wrong hands our adversaries could use them against us. When adversaries obtain them illegally, they can use them to enhance their military posture in ways that undermine global security,” said Craig Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albany Field Office, during a press conference Thursday.Federal prosecutors said an attempted purchase of electronic components from an unidentified company in New York's Northern District helped authorities uncover the alleged operation. The company reported the suspicious activity, providing investigators with a basis to pursue the case in Albany.“See something, say something,” First Assistant US Attorney John A. Sarcone III said.Prosecutors declined to identify the company or disclose what initially raised suspicions, citing the ongoing investigation.According to a criminal complaint filed in August 2025, Suvorov was the managing director and principal shareholder of GS Group Limited, an electronics company based in Hong Kong. Investigators allege that he used the company and other businesses to obtain components from American suppliers while concealing that the intended recipients were in Russia.The complaint alleges that Suvorov and his companies did not obtain the required US export licences.Investigators documented financial transactions linked to the alleged operation, including wire transfers of approximately $23,500 and $29,000 from Hong Kong to an American supplier. In a separate transaction, a bank placed on hold a payment of more than 4 million Chinese yuan from NPC Topaz to Suvorov’s Hong Kong company, according to the complaint.Authorities have not disclosed the total value of the technology allegedly obtained or the full extent of the shipments.The alleged conspiracy began in March 2022, following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, which prompted the United States to impose export restrictions on sensitive technologies to limit their potential military use by Moscow.“It reflects a larger, ongoing effort to safeguard American innovation and ensure that our most sensitive technologies do not end up in the hands of those who would use them to threaten our national security,” Tremaroli said.Authorities declined to comment on whether they believe Suvorov was acting on behalf of the Russian government or whether the alleged operation was driven by financial gain.Suvorov, who had been living in Stockholm, was transferred to US custody on Thursday after nearly a year of legal proceedings in Sweden. Federal officials said he had challenged his extradition through the Swedish legal system before being handed over to American authorities.“Just a few hours ago, Alexander Suvorov, a Russian national, stepped foot on American soil for the very first time,” Sarcone said. “Those feet were in shackles.”Federal authorities credited cooperation between the FBI, the US Department of Commerce, federal prosecutors, Swedish authorities and private businesses for advancing the investigation.You use AI every day. articles.summary: A sell-off in artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor shares has wiped out more than $1 trillion in market value from 20 of the world’s most
articles.body: A sell-off in artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor shares has wiped out more than $1 trillion in market value from 20 of the world’s most valuable technology companies in less than five days, a report has said. It attributes this to a combination of interest rate hikes, increasing AI infrastructure costs and intensifying competition. Adding to the anxiety, Chinese chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) announced plans to accelerate its memory chip manufacturing capabilities, putting fresh pressure on an already rattled global market. Elon Musk reacted to the news saying that China will be making “a LOT of RAM in 2028”, a view that could add to that pressure.The billionaire’s commentary arrives as investors grapple with growing anxiety over an impending global memory chip oversupply as early as 2029, spurred by chipmakers worldwide aggressively building out production capacity to meet AI workloads. CXMT recently said that it achieved a major architectural breakthrough to boost memory density by packing more data into tighter spaces.Here's how much Nvidia, AMD, Micron and other companies lostUS semiconductor giants and specialised cloud infrastructure providers continued to slide in premarket trading on Thursday (October 15) following a punishing Wednesday session on Wall Street.Nvidia fell 1.8%; Micron Technology dropped 4.4%; AMD slipped 3.5%; Oracle traded down 2%; Neocloud providers took sharp hits, with CoreWeave falling 5.3% and Nebius retreating 4%.Notably, the rout was not confined to US exchanges, deepening across major trading hubs in Asia and Europe. South Korean memory chip giant SK Hynix plummeted more than 10%, while rival Samsung Electronics dropped 8.73%. Related tech and component suppliers saw steep declines as well, with LG Innotek sinking 8.95%, Seoul Semiconductor sliding 9.28%, and Samsung SDI down 6.26%.In Japan, technology investment firm SoftBank Group tumbled 7.9%. Testing equipment supplier Advantest plunged nearly 14%, Tokyo Electron lost 6.45%, and Renesas Electronics fell 8%. Similarly, in Taiwan, leading contract foundry TSMC slipped 1.81%. When it comes to Europe, advanced lithography supplier ASML traded down 6.6%, ASM International sank 9.6%, Germany’s Infineon Technologies lost 9.4%, and Nokia dropped 5%.Why AI and semiconductor stocks are selling offMarket analysts and investors point to a convergence of macroeconomic headwinds, financing bottlenecks, and long-term supply threats that are eroding sentiment across the sector. Inflation has raised concerns that elevated interest rates will increase the cost of capital needed to finance massive data center and AI infrastructure deployments.Top industry leaders have voiced caution regarding capital access. On Monday, the chief executives of Broadcom and Intel warned that financing could soon become the primary headwind facing the AI boom.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Can a drug licence be suspended before a hearing? Karnataka HC explains rule
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Can a drug licensing authority suspend a pharmaceutical distributor’s licence while issuing a show-cause notice, before considering its
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Can a drug licensing authority suspend a pharmaceutical distributor’s licence while issuing a show-cause notice, before considering its response? The Karnataka high court has said the procedure under the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules requires an opportunity to respond before a suspension or cancellation order is passed.It allowed a pharmaceutical distributor to continue its business while the authorities reconsidered the matter, except for dealing with two specified injections.In an October 1, 2026, order, the court directed the authorities to treat the notice issued to Wellness Forever Chemists and Lifestyle Store as a show-cause notice, allow it to submit an additional reply and then pass appropriate orders in accordance with law.Why was the pharmaceutical distributor’s licence suspended?According to the judgment, Wellness Forever, an authorised distributor of pharmaceutical products, approached the high court after the licensing authority issued a show-cause notice-cum-suspension order on September 19, 2026.The allegation against the company was that it had procured Zavicefta Injection from Viva Pharma, which was not an authorised supply channel of Pfizer Ltd, Bengaluru, and had sold the product to various entities.The company challenged the action, arguing that the order suspending its drug licences was unlawful. It also told the court that it had filed a reply to the notice on September 21, 2026, and had appealed against the action.The licensing authority’s action was taken under Rule 66 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945, which deals with suspension and cancellation of drug licences.Can a drug licence be suspended when a show-cause notice is issued?Justice C.M. Poonacha examined Rule 66 of The Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945, which allows the licensing authority to suspend or cancel a licence if the licensee has failed to comply with licence conditions or provisions of the law. However, the rule requires the licensee to be given an opportunity to explain why such action should not be taken.The high court noted that the notice issued to the distributor did not merely communicate the allegations but also suspended its licence. It held that this was contrary to Rule 66(1), which provides for an opportunity to respond before an order of suspension or cancellation is passed.“A plain reading of sub-Rule (1) of Rule 66 of the Rules clearly indicates that the petitioner is entitled to be given a Show Cause Notice before an order of either suspension or cancellation is passed,” the court observed.The court therefore directed that the September 19 notice-cum-order be treated only as a show-cause notice. It allowed the distributor to submit an additional response, over and above the reply it had already filed, by October 8, 2026.“Having regard to the aforementioned, the impugned notice cum order dated 19.09.2026 shall be read only as a Show Cause Notice and in addition to the reply dated 21.09.2026, the petitioner shall be permitted to file an additional reply, if any, on or before 08.10.2026, consequent to which, the concerned authorities shall pass appropriate orders in accordance with law,” the high court said.The high court also noted that Rule 66 allows the licensing authority to suspend or cancel a licence either wholly or partly. It said the authorities must consider this aspect while deciding what further action to take.The court ordered that, until further action by the authorities, the distributor could continue its business in accordance with law, except for dealing with Zavicefta and Emblaveo injections.The high court disposed of the petition without preventing the authorities from taking further action in accordance with law. Its order does not amount to a final ruling on the allegation that the distributor procured the products through an unauthorised supply channel.The ruling means the company can continue its other pharmaceutical business for now, subject to the stated restrictions, while the licensing authorities consider its response and decide the next steps.

articles.title: ‘Pressured her to meet him’: UP couple kills woman’s lover, stuffs body in sack and dumps it in canal
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: A 28-year-old man was allegedly strangled with an electrical wire and beaten to death by a married couple and two of the woman’s family members
articles.body: LUCKNOW: A 28-year-old man was allegedly strangled with an electrical wire and beaten to death by a married couple and two of the woman’s family members over a relationship dispute, after which his body was stuffed into a plastic sack, transported in a Bolero vehicle and dumped near a canal in Uttar Pradesh’s Bahraich district to conceal his identity, police said.The victim, Akash Gupta, a resident of Gandhariya Buzurg village in Basti district who worked in Mumbai, was allegedly called to the house of his paramour, Poonam Devi, in Shravasti district on the evening of October 10.Her husband, Rajkumar Gupta, allegedly conspired with Poonam, her father Phoolchand and brother Anuj to kill Akash following a confrontation over the relationship, according to investigators.Police have arrested Rajkumar, 28, and Poonam, 25, while raids are underway to apprehend the other two accused, Additional Superintendent of Police (Rural) Durga Prasad Tiwari said.The case came to light on October 11, when police recovered the body of an unidentified man stuffed inside a plastic sack near the Piprahwa canal bridge in the Matera police station area of Bahraich.The investigation subsequently established the victim’s identity and led police to the couple’s home in the Malhipur police station area of neighbouring Shravasti district.According to police, the body was recovered from the banks of the Piprahwa canal on October 11. With the deceased’s identity unknown, police circulated pamphlets carrying his photograph to seek information from the public.The victim’s brother, Vikas Kasaudhan, identified the deceased as Akash Gupta after seeing his photograph. Family members reportedly told investigators that they had last spoken to Akash on the night of October 9.Following a complaint lodged by the victim’s brother, a case was registered at Matera police station on October 13, initially naming Rajkumar Gupta and Poonam Devi as accused.Investigators subsequently analysed electronic evidence, call detail records (CDRs) and CCTV footage and questioned the suspects. These investigative leads, coupled with the questioning of the arrested couple, helped police reconstruct the alleged sequence of events leading to the murder and the disposal of the body.Police said Akash, who was employed in Mumbai, was in a relationship with Poonam, a married woman living with her husband in Shravasti district.Rajkumar was allegedly aware of the relationship and had previously objected to it. According to the police investigation, a complaint concerning the relationship had been lodged around a year and a half ago at Malhipur police station and through the Uttar Pradesh Police women’s helpline, 1090.Despite the earlier complaint and warnings, Akash allegedly continued to pressurise Poonam to meet him, police said, citing the account given by Rajkumar and findings emerging during the investigation.Investigators believe the continuing dispute over the relationship was the motive behind the murder. Police have alleged that the couple decided to call Akash to their residence before the confrontation that culminated in his death.According to the police reconstruction, Rajkumar, with the help of his wife, allegedly arranged for Akash to visit their house in Shikari Chaura village under the Malhipur police station limits of Shravasti district.The meeting was reportedly arranged for around 7.30 pm on October 10, with Poonam allegedly contacting Akash and asking him to come to the house.Police said a verbal altercation broke out after Akash arrived. During the confrontation, Rajkumar, Poonam, Phoolchand and Anuj allegedly attacked him.The four accused allegedly strangled Akash using an electrical wire and assaulted him with sticks, resulting in his death, according to investigators.The involvement of Phoolchand and Anuj emerged during the investigation, police said. Both remain absconding.After the alleged murder, the accused reportedly placed Akash’s body inside a plastic sack and loaded it into a Bolero vehicle.Police said the body was then transported from Shravasti to Bahraich and dumped near the Piprahwa canal bridge in the Matera police station area. Investigators suspect the body was disposed of at the location to conceal the crime and delay identification of the victim.The sack containing the body was discovered the following day, October 11, setting off the investigation that ultimately led police to the accused.The movement of the accused and the vehicle, along with the call records and other electronic evidence, formed part of the investigation, police said.Matera police arrested Rajkumar Gupta and Poonam Devi from Chhanga crossing on October 15.The two accused are residents of Shikari Chaura village under Malhipur police station in Shravasti district. Police said both were taken into custody after investigators examined the electronic evidence, CCTV footage and call detail records and questioned them in connection with the case.Based on disclosures made by the arrested couple, police recovered an electrical wire allegedly used in the crime, two sticks and the Bolero vehicle reportedly used to transport the body.The vehicle was identified as a Bolero bearing registration number UP46E2773.Police said the necessary legal formalities were completed and the arrested accused were being sent for production before the court.Investigators have also named Phoolchand Gupta, son of Ramjiavan, and Anuj Kumar Gupta, son of Phoolchand Gupta, as accused in the case.According to police, both allegedly participated in the assault that led to Akash’s death and the subsequent disposal of his body. Police teams have been constituted and dispatched to trace and arrest them.The investigation is continuing to establish the precise role of each accused and gather further evidence relating to the alleged murder and transportation of the body.The operation was carried out under the direction of Bahraich superintendent of police Vishwajeet Srivastava, with supervision by additional superintendent of police (Rural) Durga Prasad Tiwari and Nanpara Circle Officer Chitranshu Gautam.The arrest operation was led by Matera station house officer Prempal Singh. The police team included Sub-Inspector Vijay Kumar Chaudhary, Head Constables Rajendra Modanwal and Ramjeet Yadav, Constables Sachin Singh, Sangam Yadav and Satyam Singh, and Woman Constable Muskan Maurya.Police said further action would follow as the investigation progresses and the two absconding accused are traced.The case, which initially surfaced as the recovery of an unidentified body in a sack near a canal, has now developed into a murder investigation centred on a relationship dispute, with police alleging that the victim was deliberately lured to the accused couple’s home before being killed and his body dumped in a neighbouring district.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: Illinois closes a forest road twice a year to protect migrating snakes, continuing a wildlife measure introduced in 1972
articles.summary: A quiet road in southern Illinois has an unusual distinction: it disappears from the traffic map twice a year, leaving snakes, frogs and turtles to cross
articles.body: A quiet road in southern Illinois has an unusual distinction: it disappears from the traffic map twice a year, leaving snakes, frogs and turtles to cross without the threat of passing cars. Known as Snake Road, the route runs through the Shawnee National Forest between LaRue Swamp and the LaRue-Pine Hills limestone bluffs. National Geographic's educational account describes how the road crosses a seasonal migration route used by snakes and other reptiles moving between the two habitats. Seasonal closures began in 1972, where the road is not permanently closed.The spectacle attracts wildlife enthusiasts hoping to spot dozens of snakes in their natural surroundings, while highlighting how a simple road can become a serious obstacle for migrating wildlife.The snake migration route across Snake RoadThe animals are not crossing simply because the road happens to be in their way. Their seasonal movements take them between the swamp and the rocky hills on opposite sides.During warmer months, the swamp provides feeding and living areas. When the seasons change, many reptiles head towards the limestone bluffs, where cracks, caves and rocky spaces offer places to shelter during colder weather. The return journey happens in spring.LaRue Road sits directly across this route. That creates a problem because reptiles are often drawn to the road surface when temperatures are cooler in the morning and evening. The warmed pavement can become an attractive place to rest, leaving slow-moving animals exposed to passing vehicles.The area is also home to species that are unusual this far north, including cottonmouths and southern leopard frogs.How Snake Road’s seasonal closures protect migrating reptilesThe decision to restrict traffic dates back to 1972. The road was closed during the migration periods to reduce the number of reptiles being killed by vehicles. The closures were initially unpopular with some people living nearby, according to wildlife officials quoted in reports about Snake Road. Over the years, that opposition eased as the purpose of the restriction became better understood.Today, the road is closed during the spring and autumn migrations. The exact dates cover roughly two months in each season, giving animals a vehicle-free route between the two habitats.For wildlife officials, the arrangement is fairly simple. If cars are removed from a road that thousands of reptiles need to cross, the immediate danger of being struck is removed too.Snakes, turtles and frogs share Snake Road’s migration routeDespite its name, snakes are not the only animals using the route. Frogs, toads and turtles also make the journey between the swamp and the bluffs. As reported by CBS News, there are more than 20 snake species recorded along the road during the autumn period, including three venomous species. Northern copperheads are among them, although they can be difficult to spot in southern Illinois.That does not mean visitors are surrounded by snakes every time they walk the road. Herpetologist Scott Ballard, who has studied the area, has said seeing around 20 snakes during a visit would already be a good day.The road itself is about two and a half miles for a walk there and back. People come not only to look for reptiles but also to walk through the forest and limestone landscape.How swamps and limestone cliffs create a vital wildlife routeThe geography around Snake Road is an important part of the story. On one side is LaRue Swamp, connected to the wider Mississippi River region. On the other are the LaRue-Pine Hills, where limestone cliffs rise to around 46 metres, as reported.The limestone has weathered into ridges, caves and crevices. These spaces give reptiles places where temperatures are more suitable during the colder months, while the surrounding forest and swamp provide different resources at other times of year. The road happens to run through it. Reptiles are particularly vulnerable on roads because they move slowly and often remain still when approached. A warm road surface can make the danger worse by encouraging them to stop directly in the path of traffic.Snake researcher Rich Seigel has estimated that vehicles have killed close to one in four snakes in the area studied. Across the United States, road deaths have also taken a significant toll on snakes and other reptiles.According to The National Geographic, Wildlife officials, Ballard and Deaton said that they see fewer dead reptiles on the road during the closure.Why snakes matter beyond Snake RoadSnakes are often treated as unwanted visitors, but their place in the local food chain is more practical than that reputation suggests. A single snake can consume a substantial amount of prey over the course of a year. Ballard has estimated that one snake can eat around nine pounds of rodents annually. Without predators such as snakes, rodent numbers could rise.Snakes also form part of the diet of other animals, including herons. Removing them from the ecosystem would not simply mean fewer snakes. It would alter the availability of prey and predators around them. That is one reason the migration is treated as a wildlife management issue rather than simply an unusual spectacle.What happens when people encounter a snakeVisitors can walk along Snake Road while vehicles are prohibited during seasonal closures, but encounters with wildlife require caution because some snakes in the area are venomous. Herpetologist Scott Ballard has explained that snakes generally bite when they feel surprised or threatened rather than actively seeking out people. Ballard, who has been bitten several times while working with snakes, said he had never been bitten by a venomous species. His interest in reptiles began at age 10, when he received a pet snake because he was allergic to dogs and cats. That childhood fascination eventually led him to study the snakes around Snake Road.Tips for visitors encountering snakes:Stop and slowly move a step or two away if you encounter a snake.Do not approach, handle or attempt to startle it.Observe snakes from a safe distance and allow them to move away undisturbed.A seasonal road with an unusual purposeSnake Road remains a functioning route through the Shawnee National Forest, but for several weeks each spring and autumn it serves a different purpose. The traffic signs and barriers give reptiles a rare stretch of road where vehicles are removed from their path.For visitors, the migration offers a chance to see animals moving through a landscape they otherwise might never notice. For the snakes, frogs and turtles, it is simply part of their seasonal movement between the swamp and the limestone hills.The road's unusual status comes from that overlap. It is not closed because the reptiles have taken over the road. It is closed because, for a short period each year, the road cuts directly across a route they have been using for far longer.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
